newsitem.title: UK: London emerging debt on hold for Yeltsin op news.
newsitem.headline: London emerging debt on hold for Yeltsin op news.

text.p: Emerging market debt players were holding fire in London, with the wait for news on whether Russian President Boris Yeltsin's heart operation would go ahead keeping action to a minimum.
Latin American debt held firm following yesterday's decision by the FOMC not to raise US interest rates, but players are still digesting the implications, looking ahead.

In the meantime dealers were keeping an eye on today's GKO auction in Russia, with early reports saying the January 22 and May 21 maturities were very well subscribed, with strong interest from foreign buyers.
"That should provide a better bid for Vnesh," said one dealer at a European firm here. "But mostly the market is waiting for the outcome of the decision on Yeltsin's operation."
Doctors began meeting at a Moscow hospital today to decide whether Yeltsin's planned heart surgery should go ahead, and when.
"If it comes out that the operation is going ahead next week, that will reduce the uncertainty," the dealer said.
Russian dollar Vnesh was up 1/4 at 63-1/2 at 1000 GMT, but traders said the price was still bouncing around.
The MinFin 3 took a bit of a hammering this morning on fears that the planned launch of Russia's three to five year dollar eurobond may be delayed amid fears over Yeltsin's health, traders said.
But by mid-morning it had recovered 1/8 from last night's close, quoted at 76-1/8 in London trading.
Instead Bulgaria showed some strength in an otherwise lacklustre market. IABs were a touch firmer, quoted at 44-7/8.
But one trader said this was largely the result of a short squeeze after clients switched out of Russian Vnesh loans and into Bulgarian paper earlier in the week.
Bulgaria this week announced a number of bank stabilisation measures, including the placing of nine problem banks under special supervision and raising interest rate to a record 300 percent high.
The moves were designed to persuade the IMF to release the second $115 million tranche of a promised loan, but traders remain sceptical.

"Bulgaria is in a better state than one or two weeks ago -- raising interest rates stablised the currency, but it will hurt domestic banks and growth," said one eastern European debt trader. Players say they are still unclear on whether the IMF will release the loan.

Elsewhere, Latin America was mostly flat. Mexican Pars were quoted unchanged at 68-7/8, Argentine FRBs were flat at 57-3/8, and Brazil Cs were also steady at 69-1/8. --Caroline Brothers, London Newsroom +44 171 542 2734
